question: Among patients biopsied for PDAC PDO testing, do biopsy modality, tumor cellularity and time from biopsy to first test predict a usable result before treatment selection, beyond standard clinical factors?
biological_value: minor: could identify sampling and turnaround bottlenecks that determine which patients can actually benefit from functional testing, but this is primarily an implementation decision rather than a new mechanism.
closest_prior_art: HOPE already reports organoid growth predictors, low testing yield and long turnaround (P14/D01); 2025 PDAC work reports 58% PDO establishment (P20/D02).
exact_increment: Use patient-level actionable-time test completion as the endpoint, retaining failures and biopsy repeats; test whether preanalytic variables add decision value beyond current growth-only summaries.
independent_unit: Patient; biopsy specimens and organoid wells nested within patient.
primary_endpoint: Patient-level usable PDO result returned by an actionable treatment decision date, with time-to-result and assay failure retained.
comparator: HOPE modality/cellularity growth table and simple clinical baseline; no complex score unless incremental value is demonstrated.
evaluation_design: Reconstruct the complete patient/sample chronology, split/group by patient only, and seek a second prospective PDAC PDO cohort; do not use 75 biopsy observations as 75 independent patients.
minimal_decisive_test: Obtain the complete HOPE workbook and patient-level treatment-decision/test-time linkage; confirm the same measurements and endpoint exist in a second PDO cohort.
success_gate: A small set of preanalytic features predicts timely usable tests after patient grouping and replicates in an independent cohort strongly enough to change biopsy or trial-enrollment practice.
revise_or_stop_gate: If the full file exposes only growth status without patient-level treatment-window linkage, keep this descriptive; stop if HOPE already covers the exact increment or too few patients succeed for a stable estimate.
main_risks: Only 12/76 participants achieved testing; selection by survival/tissue sufficiency; repeated biopsies; growth status is not clinical benefit; modest biological discovery.
rank_or_rejection_reason: Most accessible evidence, but only an implementation/feasibility lead and low biological novelty; do not treat as the leading project candidate. Consider only if full patient-level timing/outcomes and an independent cohort exist.

family: Ex-vivo assay endpoint and persister biology
question: Across medically relevant patient-derived cancer models exposed to a defined drug pulse, does early cell-resolved death commitment relate to subsequent regrowth after washout, and where measured, does it add information beyond bulk ATP viability or growth-rate inhibition?
biological_value: well_motivated: an acute bulk viability readout may hide a small population capable of repopulating after treatment, so the result could change how ex-vivo resistance is defined.
closest_prior_art: P20 uses 3-day CellTiter-Glo/AUC/IC50; P05 (PROSPERO) already studies acute CyTOF functional markers versus later viability, with no direct clinical correlation and separate sample sets not verified; R02 reviews cell-type/endpoint limits. Established growth-rate inhibition (GR) metrics (Hafner et al., 2016) are a necessary comparator; exact primary citation and fractional-killing/washout/rechallenge literature remain to be verified before a novelty claim.
exact_increment: Match early cell-resolved death fate to post-washout reproductive outgrowth under the same dose and biological model, beyond the acute-marker-versus-later-viability comparison already in PROSPERO; use ATP/GR comparisons only when measured and do not substitute another AUC, PK threshold or clinical-response score.
independent_unit: Patient-derived line/patient; cells, doses, timepoints and wells nested.
primary_endpoint: Model-level regrowth after washout (e.g., colony formation, outgrowth fraction or growth recovery), paired with early cell-resolved death commitment; cells and wells remain nested within biological models.
comparator: 72-hour bulk ATP viability plus growth-rate-normalized GR effect; report fractional killing/death kinetics where available.
evaluation_design: For an ex-vivo biological claim, compare donor lines as independent units with time- and dose-matched assays; clinical prediction is not required. Hold out patients/lines, never wells.
minimal_decisive_test: First locate a public processed dataset in a medically relevant cancer model with early cell-death and post-washout regrowth linked by model/donor; include non-organoid patient-derived systems. ATP/GR is a comparator only if measured. If none exists, parent must separately decide whether experimental access exists before a pilot.
success_gate: Early death commitment has a reproducible relationship with later regrowth across independent biological models under a prespecified dose/time comparison; claim added value over ATP/GR only if those endpoints are measured.
revise_or_stop_gate: Stop the computational route if no matched accessible dataset exists; stop an incremental-comparator claim if measured GR/fractional-killing metrics already explain regrowth, and stop the broader biological claim if the relationship fails across independent models.
main_risks: No matched public dataset found yet; organoid access and assay resources unknown; culture growth/dropout, stromal contamination, dose timing and washout may confound; clinical translation is a separate claim.
rank_or_rejection_reason: Biological-priority lead for a bounded feasibility test, not a project rank: distinct from generic score work but fails the current accessible-data gate; include non-organoid patient-derived models only if they have matched endpoints.

question: In AML patients, does drug-induced dynamic-BH3 priming of CD123-defined malignant subpopulations predict remission beyond bulk priming for the same treatment panel?
biological_value: potentially_meaningful: cell-subpopulation vulnerabilities could affect treatment selection and clonal survival.
closest_prior_art: The 2025 bioRxiv preprint reports prospective DBP on myeloblasts from 92 AML patients, within-patient CD123-expression priming differences, and remission prediction (P04/D09); Beat AML studies already link measured ex-vivo response to patient outcome (P01/P02/D06).
exact_increment: No supported increment remains for the broad question: the closest preprint directly addresses both the subpopulation contrast and outcome prediction. A different, narrowly defined discordant treatment-response mechanism would require separate evidence.
independent_unit: Patient; CD123 subpopulations, cells and technical wells nested.
primary_endpoint: Observed remission following a specified treatment, analyzed at patient level.
comparator: Bulk DBP response and established AML clinical/genetic prognostic factors.
evaluation_design: Would require patient-grouped independent cohort with the same fixed drug panel and prespecified remission definition; the preprint’s own cohort is not external validation.
minimal_decisive_test: Read peer-reviewed status, methods/splits and data supplement after access is available; identify a truly independent cohort or a treatment-specific contrast not already reported.
success_gate: Only proceed if external, grouped records exist and a distinct treatment mechanism is not already tested.
revise_or_stop_gate: Stop the broad version: it is directly described in the preprint; revisit only for an externally testable, mechanism-specific discordance.
main_risks: Preprint not peer reviewed; full methods/supplement and data not inspected; treatment selection confounding; within-patient cells cannot inflate n.
rank_or_rejection_reason: Rejected as stated due direct overlap, despite biological value.

family: CAR-T antigen escape and leukemia lineage plasticity
question: Across paired diagnosis/relapse samples after CD19-directed immunotherapy, do genetic clone markers show whether a myeloid lineage-switch relapse arose from a pre-existing alternate-lineage clone or conversion of the original B-lineage leukemia?
biological_value: well_motivated: identifying the mechanism could change monitoring and antigen-targeting strategies.
closest_prior_art: A B-ALL single-patient study reports pre-existing CD19-negative subclones (P09/D04); a mouse study shows CAR pressure can induce lineage switch (P10); Project EVOLVE is a 2025 international analysis of post-immunotherapy lineage switch (P19).
exact_increment: Require patient-level genetic/lineage evidence to distinguish clone selection from phenotypic conversion across paired cases; RNA trajectory alone is not ancestry evidence. Project EVOLVE is a close competitor, and its exact case-level increment remains unverified.
independent_unit: Patient; cells, samples and technical assays nested.
primary_endpoint: Genetic continuity or divergence between diagnostic leukemia and lineage-switched relapse, with baseline clone detectability.
comparator: Morphology/flow antigen-loss classification and published P09/P10/P19 case definitions.
evaluation_design: Use independent paired diagnosis/relapse patients; stratify by immunotherapy and require lineage/genetic evidence; no expression-only pseudo-lineage tracing.
minimal_decisive_test: Read the full Project EVOLVE case inclusion and molecular evidence tables; check for public patient-linked diagnosis/relapse genomic records and an independent case series.
success_gate: An independent cohort with paired molecular records supports a mechanism-specific baseline predictor or surveillance target not already reported.
revise_or_stop_gate: Stop broad prevalence/ancestry claims if only published case series summaries or one patient are accessible; do not infer clone ancestry from pseudotime.
main_risks: Strong existing prior art; rare events; publication/selection bias; no denominator; specimen identifiers and data access unresolved.
rank_or_rejection_reason: Not ranked: broad lineage-switch field has clear prior work, but the specific paired-clone-ancestry increment is unresolved because Project EVOLVE was not close-read and no public paired records were inspected.

question: Among tumor neoantigen candidates with direct evidence of natural peptide presentation and patient-matched T-cell assays, can presentation failure be separated from TCR-engagement failure to explain false-positive immunogenicity predictions?
biological_value: well_motivated: a prediction that confuses display with T-cell recognition can nominate antigens that tumor-reactive T cells do not actually see.
closest_prior_art: TESLA measures patient-matched T-cell recognition, but its “presented” label is a model filter (<34 nM binding, >33 TPM tumor abundance, >1.4 h predicted stability), not direct MS evidence of natural presentation (parent source check); NeoScore and Neo-intline reuse related benchmarks. BigMHC 2023 (DOI 10.1038/s42256-023-00694-6) trains on MS presentation and transfers to immunogenicity, so it is relevant prior art, not proof the exact question is solved.
exact_increment: Partition failure between directly observed natural tumor peptide presentation and patient-matched T-cell recognition, evaluated by patient-held-out splits; TESLA’s presentation filter is derived, and direct MS plus T-cell assays may not coexist in accessible records.
independent_unit: Patient/tumor; multiple pMHCs nested within patient.
primary_endpoint: Measured patient-matched T-cell activation/recognition, with direct presentation evidence where available.
comparator: Published TESLA experimental calls and existing NeoScore/Neo-intline predictors.
evaluation_design: Patient-held-out or tumor-held-out evaluation; separate pMHC-level assays from patient-level replication; independent study required for generalization.
minimal_decisive_test: Open the smallest Synapse TESLA file; verify per-patient keys, actual 608/37 inclusion and availability of presentation and T-cell assay layers; compare later model training/evaluation subsets exactly.
success_gate: A measurable presentation-versus-TCR-engagement failure mode remains under patient-held-out evaluation and changes which candidate antigens are nominated.
revise_or_stop_gate: Stop if the underlying file lacks patient/sample keys or separates no presentation and recognition assays; stop the novelty claim if P06 or later work already partitions these errors.
main_risks: No direct natural-presentation label is verified in TESLA; presentation and recognition layers may come from different samples; exact cohort grouping and public file access unverified; later predictors reuse TESLA; clinical response is a separate endpoint.
rank_or_rejection_reason: Biological-priority lead for a bounded data/prior-art test, not a project rank: no natural-presentation layer or patient-grouped Synapse rows were verified; proceed only if a linked direct MS/T-cell dataset exists.

family: CAR-T infusion-product state and relapse phenotype
question: Among patients with CD19-positive relapse after CAR-T therapy, do infusion-product T-cell states associate with relapse despite retained tumor antigen, after separating antigen-negative relapse and baseline tumor features?
biological_value: potentially_meaningful: it distinguishes immune-effector failure from tumor antigen escape and may guide product selection.
closest_prior_art: P11 directly analyzes single-cell CAR-T infusion product and determinants of CD19-positive relapse in a 12-patient ALL cohort; P09 and P19 cover tumor antigen/lineage escape.
exact_increment: Only an independent patient cohort with matched product state, tumor antigen at relapse and pre-treatment tumor features could extend the existing product-state analysis.
independent_unit: Patient; infusion-product cells and tumor cells nested.
primary_endpoint: Relapse phenotype (CD19-positive versus CD19-negative/lineage-switched) with measured tumor antigen and product phenotype.
comparator: P11’s published infusion-product substate findings and tumor antigen status alone.
evaluation_design: Independent matched CAR-T cohort, grouped by patient and therapy/product; separate cell-level abundance from patient-level relapse outcome.
minimal_decisive_test: Verify P11’s matching fields and later independent cohorts; determine whether public data include paired tumor antigen status and CAR-T infusion-product single-cell records.
success_gate: An independent patient-level interaction between product state and retained tumor antigen predicts a distinct relapse mode beyond P11.
revise_or_stop_gate: Stop if product and tumor data are not paired or the independent cohort does not record relapse phenotype.
main_risks: Direct overlap with P11; n=12 source; survivor/relapse selection; missing paired tumor samples.
rank_or_rejection_reason: Rejected as stated because the closest primary paper already addresses product state and CD19-positive relapse.

question: Across patient-derived paired pre/post-treatment tumor samples, which cell-state changes consistently distinguish responders from nonresponders across cancer types and regimens?
biological_value: minor: a broad atlas question, but a broad signature or trajectory catalogue is not a distinct biological discovery by itself.
closest_prior_art: The 2026 peer-reviewed scCT-DB reports 266 paired datasets and 48 opposite-response pairs, supports cross-dataset response comparisons and longitudinal analysis (P17/D08); P12 studies cellular adaptation along a resistance continuum.
exact_increment: No generic increment remains. A new question would have to specify one mechanism, a defensible independent unit, treatment timing and evidence beyond expression-state association.
independent_unit: Patient for clinical data; cells nested within patient/sample.
primary_endpoint: Prespecified patient-level response-associated change in a mechanistically defined cell state, not a post hoc all-cell-type signature.
comparator: scCT-DB’s response-vs-nonresponse and longitudinal perturbation modules; P12 resistance-continuum study.
evaluation_design: Would require patient-level grouping, matched treatment/timing, cancer/regimen strata and independent dataset validation; do not treat cells as patient replicates.
minimal_decisive_test: Only reopen for a named mechanism with an accessible scCT-DB subset and actual dataset-level patient/outcome metadata not already analyzed by the resource.
success_gate: A specific state mechanism replicates across independent patient cohorts and is supported by perturbation or lineage evidence.
revise_or_stop_gate: Stop the generic atlas/signature proposal; pre/post expression alone cannot establish lineage or causality.
main_risks: Resource and dataset overlap; heterogenous response definitions; dataset/patient imbalance; portal inaccessible; expression-derived states are not observed lineage.
rank_or_rejection_reason: Rejected as broad question because current 2026 resource directly provides this class of comparison.

question: In PDAC PDO pharmacotyping, does concordance differ between metastatic RECIST response and resected-disease relapse outcomes, and does biopsy-to-test delay help explain discordant patient-level predictions?
biological_value: potentially_meaningful: separating treatment setting and endpoint may show whether an ex-vivo assay measures intrinsic drug response consistently or only under particular disease contexts.
closest_prior_art: HOPE directly links PDO sensitivity to clinical outcomes but has 12/76 patients tested (P14/D01); P20 reports 13 first-line matched cases with mixed resected/metastatic outcome definitions; P16 is a larger advanced-PDAC functional precision study; P21 is an access-limited later lead.
exact_increment: Analyze clinically distinct observed outcomes separately and treat assay delay as a timing modifier, not as a new drug-response score; ensure discordant cases are not collapsed into a single sensitive/resistant label.
independent_unit: Patient; biopsy, PDO dose-response wells and treatment episodes nested.
primary_endpoint: Patient-level concordance/discordance between measured PDO regimen response and prespecified clinical endpoint, stratified by treatment setting and time to test.
comparator: Published single-agent and multi-drug AUC/PK classification in P20; HOPE’s reported patient-linked responses and available P16 study endpoint.
evaluation_design: Require patient-level response records and independent cohort with same endpoint/setting; do not pool RECIST, CA19-9 and relapse without prespecified mapping.
minimal_decisive_test: Verify whether P20 supplements and P16/P21 expose case-level assay plus clinical labels; document cohort overlap, disease setting, timing and response definition before any modeling.
success_gate: A disease-setting or assay-delay effect on concordance remains after patient-level grouping, endpoint harmonization and independent replication, and changes interpretation of pharmacotyping.
revise_or_stop_gate: Stop if only aggregate accuracy is available, if groups contain too few patients, or if endpoint definitions cannot be separated; do not tune AUC/PK scores.
main_risks: Thirteen matched first-line cases in P20; different outcome windows and disease contexts; accessible rows not yet verified; 2025 score paper directly closes generic metric improvement.
rank_or_rejection_reason: Clinically interpretable but lower biological priority than C02/C05; reserve for feasibility only if patient-level records separate disease setting, endpoint and testing time.
